judgments.reasoning_cat1: The territory definitions are transcribed as scrambled columns and Territory 1 is defined as 'the remainder of the states ... not listed in Territories 2', a residual definition whose content depends entirely on a list that is itself garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is superseded by Rating Schedule-A (c060) and then Schedule-B (c080), each with a different state list, so which territory table applies to a policy depends on its effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Effective January 1, 1904' is a plain mechanical error in the operative effective date, and 'net profit accruing to the REINSURED' does not match the defined term, while the proviso limiting the article to 'the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits as respects each policy' is left unexplained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Accounting Schedule (c021) still credits and charges the whole account with no mechanism to isolate the first $1,000,000 of limits, and 'net profit' is defined in c024 as excess of credits over charges, not profit 'accruing to the REINSURED'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'loss arising out of the operation of a teaching hospital' leaves 'teaching hospital' undefined and, by dropping the original words 'by the insured', makes the exclusion's subject uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Article II(a) (c005) only for policies effective on or after July 1, 1995, so the two versions coexist in the instrument and must be sequenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 350-bed threshold is numerically precise, though the defined 'total beds' again qualifies only acute care beds as 'occupied'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes the 250-bed version (c006) for later policies, an intentional but date-sensitive inconsistency within the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of named counties with no general catch-all; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It silently drops Cuyahoga County (excluded under c008) while Rating Schedules A and B (c061, c081) price Cleveland accounts as Territory 3, implying that risk is now rated and covered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The self-insured proviso and the layered percentages are dense but arithmetically coherent as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is itself deleted and replaced by Amendment No. 4 (c076), and its 'self-insured' premise still sits against Article I's requirement of underlying insurance (c001).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line substitution instruction; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 2 (c066) later amends Schedule-A, which Amendment No. 4 (c077) then deletes entirely, so the chain of substitutions has to be traced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In all other respects not inconsistent herewith' is a vague reconciliation formula that does not say who decides what is inconsistent or which text prevails.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That formula is precisely what has to be applied to reconcile Amendment No. 1's contingent-commission cap (c052) with the untouched Accounting Schedule (c021).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A rating table of multipliers; the CRNA '5-10' range is the only open figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the original schedule (c050) and is later repeated again in Schedule-B (c079) without material change.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-column list is transcribed out of alignment, and the Territory 2 entry 'All areas except Wayne and Oakland County — Michigan' is a state not named in the Territory 1 residual list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (d) as amended (c055) removes Wayne and Oakland County Michigan policies from the agreement altogether, and Amendment No. 2 (c066) rewrites this Territory 1 paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two named locations; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Alaska appears here although it is absent from every Territory 1 state list and from Article I's scope, a mild loose end.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three fixed multipliers; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Schedule-B multipliers (c082); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entry is unintelligible as transcribed — the label is lost and only 'Applied to premium developed in OBE rating. -125' survives, so neither the factor nor its sign can be applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The corresponding Schedule-B entries (c084, c092, c098) give different figures (-125, 25, -15) for the same Indiana/Wisconsin factor, which is hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean ladder of claims-made credits by year with a stated mature rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule-B (c085) states different credits (and repeats 35% for both the 2nd and 3rd year), so the two schedules diverge across amendments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The percentages are printed before the categories they belong to, so which credit attaches to which class of hospital is not clear on the face of the entry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule-B's version (c087) supplies the same figures with the pairing intact, which resolves it but only by reference to the later schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward substitution of a state list; only the OCR-mangled 'Webraska' is odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 (c077) deletes Schedule-A wholesale and substitutes Schedule-B, whose Territory 1 omits Iowa and South Dakota — so this amendment's addition silently disappears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The boilerplate 'not inconsistent herewith' carries the same vagueness as its siblings but governs only a territory list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its practical effect is undone by the later wholesale replacement of Schedule-A (c077).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A name-change substitution with a stated effective date; nothing open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Later documents (c076, c093, c095, c099) use OHIC and 'REINSURED' interchangeably, consistently with this amendment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same boilerplate reconciliation formula, here attached to a purely nominal change.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the agreement is inconsistent with a name change.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It introduces a 'claims-conversion basis' that the agreement nowhere defines (only the Schedule-B factor in c086 alludes to it), and it retains the contestable 'excess of underlying insurance which afford limits not less than' formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Article I (c001) only for policies effective on or after October 1, 1996, and must be read with the new Schedule entries (c071), the replaced Article III (c076) and the Stipulation of Termination (c099).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The added entries are duplicative and self-contradictory in form — 'Nursing Homes and Outpatient Facilities Professional Liability' is listed, then 'Outpatient Facility Professional Liability' again with the same limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The added coverages must be matched to Article III(b)'s separate $10,000,000 limit for Nursing Home and Outpatient Facility business (c076) and to the new exclusions (c072-c075).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'nursing homes with more than five locations unless the primary Commercial General Liability and Professional Liability limits apply per location' hinges on the undefined notion of a 'location' and on how the primary limits are read to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the Nursing Home coverage added by c070/c071 and the separate limit in c076(b) without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'fire resistive and sprinklered' are underwriting terms of art left undefined, and 'exceed five stories in height' is otherwise precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the other nursing home exclusions added by the same amendment; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'surgicenters, emergicenters, hospices or laboratories' is a bare list of undefined facility types with no definitional anchor anywhere in the agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same amendment adds Outpatient Facility Professional Liability coverage (c070, c071) and a Facility Rating section (c093), so the exclusion and the grant of outpatient cover pull against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion of 'outpatient facilities with employed physicians who provide patient care' followed by a carve-back for 'medical directors and other administrative positions which may be staffed by a physician' creates an obvious boundary problem for a medical director who also treats patients.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the outpatient coverage newly added by c070/c071 and overlaps the facility exclusion in c074.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence 'As respects claims made policy forms, each claim shall be deemed an occurrence hereunder' is a deeming rule with real aggregation consequences against an annual aggregate, and the self-insured proviso is again dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes c012 and c056, sits against the annual aggregate structure and the Schedule of Underlying Limits' 'each medical incident' basis (c002/c071), and must be read with the loss definition in c013.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single substitution instruction; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It wipes out Schedule-A including the Territory 1 change made by Amendment No. 2 (c066), while Article VI (c018) still refers simply to 'the Rating Schedule'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same vague 'not inconsistent herewith' reconciliation formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only instrument for reconciling the substantially rewritten Article I and Article III with untouched provisions such as Article V (c017) and Article VII (c020/c021).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A rating table; only the CRNA '5-10' range is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reproduces c050/c059 without material change.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Territory 1 is again a residual ('the remainder of the states ... not listed in Territories 2 or 3') and the city/county column is transcribed out of alignment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drops Iowa and South Dakota, which Amendment No. 2 (c066) had expressly added to Territory 1, and drops the Michigan and Washington entries from Territory 2 (c060).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two named entries; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Alaska and Cleveland are rated here although Alaska appears in no Territory 1 list; a small loose end, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three fixed multipliers; nothing open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c062; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'incidental owned automobile exposure' and 'Any Owned Ambulances involved in emergency runs' are both judgement-laden triggers for an additional charge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c001/c070) brings Automobile Liability within the agreement with a $1,000,000 underlying limit (c002), and this rating rule assumes no separate charge in most cases; workable together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The figures are bare and unexplained ('-125' and '25') with no statement of whether they are factors, percentages or credits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Nursing Home and Facility versions of the same entry (c092, c098) give '25/258' and '-15/25', which cannot all be reconciled as the same factor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 2nd and 3rd year both show a 35% credit, which is almost certainly a transcription or drafting error in a ladder that otherwise decreases monotonically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule-A's ladder (c064) reads 55/45/35/25/18, so the replacement schedule diverges in a way that affects premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'an extended reporting endorsement will be issued at no additional cost' is a firm promise but says nothing about limits, and 'claims-conversion' remains undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c003) provides that a discovery period or extended reporting endorsement is part of the policy period 'subject to the provision that a separate limit of liability may apply', which sits awkwardly with a free endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two credits, each tied to a stated class, with an express carve-out for minimum premiums.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It corrects the pairing problem in c065; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'OHIC's Manual GL and Professional Liability Premium (before application of experience and schedule rating)' is a definite computational base, though it depends on an external manual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'OHIC' where the parallel Facility section (c093) says 'the REINSURED'S Manual', the same entity after the Amendment No. 3 name change (c068).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'can be modified by schedule credit or debit at the REINSURED'S discretion but not to exceed 25% for a credit' caps credits but leaves debits uncapped and the discretion unconstrained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Facility counterpart (c095) is identically drafted but attributed to 'OHIC'; no substantive conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of limits and the list of factors are printed in separate blocks with the 'Minimum Premiums' heading intruding between them, so the pairing of factor to layer is not clear on the face of the entry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Article III(b) limit for Nursing Home business is $10,000,000 (c076), which matches the 'next $9,000,000' structure here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Each million in limits is subject to a minimum premium of $1,000,000' is on its face an error — a minimum premium equal to the entire limit of cover — and the block otherwise repeats the excess factors rather than stating premiums.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VI (c018) makes premium 'subject to the applicable minimum premium specified in the Rating Schedule', so this erroneous figure is given operative effect elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The figures '25' and '258' are unexplained and the second is plainly a mis-transcription of a charge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: They contradict the corresponding Hospital and Facility entries (c084: -125/25; c098: -15/25) for the same Indiana/Wisconsin factor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 25% factor applied to a stated premium base, with a listed automobile load; only the external manual reference is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The private passenger load is $80 here but $50 in the Nursing Home section (c088) — different rating sections, so not necessarily inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise rate-per-$1,000-receipts ladder; the only softness is what counts as an 'Imaging (MRI) risk'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the excess factors in c096 and the automobile cross-reference to c093; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Caps credits at 25% but leaves debits unlimited and discretion unqualified; otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says 'at OHIC's discretion' where the parallel nursing home provision (c089) says 'at the REINSURED'S discretion' — the same party under Amendment No. 3 (c068).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean ladder of percentages applied to 'the modified First Million price'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the First Million definition in c093 and the credit rule in c095.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The first million is subject to a minimum premium of $1,500,000' states a minimum premium exceeding the layer of cover it prices — an evident mechanical error that changes the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VI (c018) makes premium subject to 'the applicable minimum premium specified in the Rating Schedule', so the erroneous figure has operative bite, and it does not track the Nursing Home minimums in c091.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The factor is given as '-is' (unreadable) with a charge of 25, so the entry cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from the Hospital and Nursing Home versions of the same factor (c084, c092) without explanation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Termination 'with respect to loss under policies issued on or after January 1, 1998' keys the cut-off to issuance, whereas the agreement elsewhere speaks of policies 'becoming effective' or 'in force', and it does not say what happens to earlier policies' run-off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XI (c033) already prescribes a run-off on cancellation ('all policies in force ... until their individual natural expiration or next anniversary ... 12 months plus odd time'), and Article VII (c025) defers contingent commission past termination, so the three must be read together to fix the parties' continuing obligations.
